transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. Um, well, I guess I'm here because... I've been having some thoughts lately that I'm really not very proud of. I hope it's okay to just be honest about it with you? 

I just keep thinking that... well, that maybe it would be better if I just didn't wake up in the morning. I know that sounds terrible, and I'm really sorry, I don't mean to sound dramatic or anything. It's just... I've messed up so much with my family, and with the guys on my flooring crew at work, and sometimes I just feel like dying would be the fair punishment for what I've done to them. 

Is that... does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question right.
Have you had any specific plans about how you might end your life, or have you thought about taking any steps toward hurting yourself?

Oh, no, please don't worry. I haven't made any real plans or taken any steps like that. I'm so sorry if I alarmed you, I really didn't mean to make it sound like an emergency. 

It's just... like I was trying to explain a second ago, it's more of a heavy feeling that just sits with me. I just keep having those thoughts that it would be better if I didn't wake up. It's not that I'm actively trying to hurt myself, it just feels like... well, like dying would be the fair punishment for everything I've put my family and my crew through. 

But I haven't planned out how to do anything. I'm trying really hard to be good and stay safe. I hope that puts your mind at ease a little bit? I really don't want to be a burden to you.
Have you noticed yourself losing interest or taking less pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy, like hobbies or time with family and friends?

Um, well... I guess I have been a little less active lately. I really don't want to sound lazy or anything, I promise I usually work really hard. But... yeah, I suppose I have. 

I used to do a lot of things. Like, I used to paint, and I'd cook these big meals, and I'd even go for a run before heading to my flooring jobs. I used to always show up for my theater rehearsals, too. But now... I hope this doesn't make me sound awful, but... those things just feel like chores from somebody else's life. I just... I find that I don't really care if I miss them anymore. 

Which is terrible, I know. I really should care, and I feel so guilty that I've been dropping the ball. Does that... does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Have you found yourself feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, lately?

Um, I don't... I don't think so? I mean, I hope I'm not coming across as depressed or, you know, ungrateful or anything. I really try to keep a smile on and be pleasant for everyone. 

I guess... I mean, I do have those heavy thoughts I mentioned, but I wouldn't say I'm just sitting around feeling sad all day every day. I really try my best to keep going and not let things get me down too much. I don't want to be a downer for the people around me, you know? 

So, no, I don't think I feel depressed most of the day. Is that... is that okay? I hope I'm not misunderstanding what you're asking.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately, like eating much less or much more than usual?

Um, well... I hope you don't think I'm doing it on purpose or anything, because I know how important it is to take care of myself. But, um, I guess I haven't been eating as much as I should. 

It's not that I'm trying to lose weight or be difficult, I promise! It's just... most days I kind of forget to eat until it gets really late. Or, if I do try to make something, I'll take a few bites and my stomach just feels sort of sick, so I stop. 

I did notice my work pants are getting a little loose, which I feel bad about because I don't want to look unprofessional on the job. I really am trying to eat when I can, though. I hope that's not too concerning? I'll try to do better if you think I need to.
Have you found yourself feeling guilty or like you're a burden to others more often lately?

Um... oh, I really hate to admit this. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around throwing a pity party for myself, I really don't. But... yes. I guess I do feel that way a lot. 

I just... I can't help but feel like everything going wrong is my fault. Like... my husband hasn't been doing well lately, and I keep thinking it's because of me. And the crew I work with... we lost some jobs, and some of the clients' floors got messed up, and... I just feel like I'm the reason for all of it. Like I just poison everything I touch right now. 

It makes me feel like I just deserve whatever bad things happen to me, you know? Because I'm dragging everyone else down. I'm really sorry, I know that sounds so dramatic and I shouldn't think like that. I really try to be helpful and do a good job, I promise. Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding too crazy or anything.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the flip side, feeling restless or unable to sit still lately?

Um, no, I don't think so? I mean, I hope I haven't been acting strange or anything. I really try to keep my energy up and stay focused, especially at work. Installing flooring is pretty physical, so I have to keep moving, you know? 

I haven't noticed myself slowing down or, like, pacing around or anything like that. I really try to stay steady and just do what needs to be done so I'm not a bother to anyone. If I have been acting different, nobody's mentioned it to me. Is... is there something you're looking for with that? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Can you tell me if there have been days when you felt down or hopeless most of the day, and how often that happened over the past couple of weeks?

Um... I really hope you don't think I'm just complaining, because I know I have a lot to be thankful for. I really try to keep a positive attitude, I promise I do. But... um, I guess I have had some days where I just feel... sad. 

I wouldn't say hopeless, exactly. That sounds so extreme, and I don't want to sound like I'm giving up or anything. I still go to work and try to do a good job on the floors. But... yeah, maybe for the last couple of weeks, I've just felt a little more down than usual on most days. 

It's just hard to shake sometimes, even when I'm trying my best to smile and be pleasant for the clients and the crew. I really am trying to snap out of it, though. I hope it's okay that I feel this way right now? I know I should be stronger than this.
Have you noticed that you’ve been feeling more tired or low on energy lately, even if you’re not doing anything physically demanding?

Um... well, I really hate to complain about being tired, because I know everyone gets tired, especially working construction, right? I mean, it's just part of the job, and I don't want to sound lazy or like I'm not pulling my weight with the crew. I really do try to push through it. 

But... I guess lately, it's been a little harder than usual. It's embarrassing to admit, but... sometimes, by the time I carry just one box of tile in from the truck, or even just sit down and answer a couple of messages from clients... my body just feels so heavy. Like wet cement, almost. And my head just gets so exhausted that I can't even figure out simple things, like which pattern to lay next. 

I'm so sorry, I know that sounds terrible. I really am trying to keep my energy up, I just... I don't know why I'm getting so worn out so fast right now. I hope you don't think I'm just making excuses to get out of working hard. Do you think it's normal to feel that drained from such little things?
Can you tell me if most days, for the past two weeks or more, you've felt down or sad for most of the day, even when nothing particularly bad was happening?

Um... I know we just talked about this a little bit, and I really, really don't want to sound like a broken record or like I'm whining. I know I said I've been feeling sad, but... I don't know if I'd say it's been most of the day, every day for two whole weeks. That sounds so... so bad, doesn't it? 

I mean, I still have good moments. Like when I finish a really tricky tile pattern and the client is happy, I feel good about that. I always try to focus on the good things so I don't let myself get too down. I wouldn't want anyone to think I'm just sitting around moping all day for no reason. 

I guess I just... I try to stay busy so I don't notice it as much. I'm sorry, I'm probably not explaining this very well. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answer without making it sound worse than it is. Does that make sense? I hope I'm being helpful.
Can you tell me if there have been times over the past two weeks when, even when nothing bad was happening, you still felt sad or down for most of the day, nearly every day?

Um... I feel like we're kind of going in circles, and I really hope I'm not frustrating you by not giving a clear enough answer. I promise I'm trying to be as helpful as I can. 

I just... I don't think it's been *every* single day, or even nearly every day. Like I said, I really try to keep my chin up and focus on the work. I mean, if I was just sad all day, every day, I wouldn't be able to get any floors done, right? And I really pride myself on doing a good job for the clients. 

So, no, I wouldn't say it's been that constant. I try really hard not to let myself get stuck in a rut like that. I hope that's the right answer? I just don't want to make it sound like I'm completely falling apart when I'm still trying my best to hold it together.

Can you tell me if you’ve had a period of time in the past two weeks where you felt down or lost interest in things for most of the day, more days than not, even when there wasn’t a specific reason for it?

Um... well, the losing interest part... I really hate to admit this, because I don't want you to think I'm just giving up or being lazy outside of work. I promise I'm usually a very active person. 

I used to do a lot. Like, I used to paint, and I'd always cook these really big meals... I'd even go for a run before heading to a job site in the mornings, and I'm supposed to show up for theater rehearsals... 

But... yeah, I guess I have kind of stopped doing all of that. It's so embarrassing to say out loud, but lately... I don't know, all those things just feel like chores from somebody else's life. I haven't been going to rehearsal, and the worst part is—and I feel so, so guilty admitting this—I don't even really care if I miss them right now. 

Which is awful, right? I know I should care. People are counting on me. I hope I'm answering your question right, I just... I really want you to know I'm not usually like this. I want to be doing those things, I just can't seem to care about them right now. Is it normal to just... lose the drive for things you used to love like that?
Can you tell me if, over the past two weeks, there have been days when you felt down or sad for most of the day, even when nothing bad was happening?

Um... I feel terrible, I really do, because I know you keep asking about feeling sad or down, and I feel like I'm just being difficult by not giving you a straight "yes." I promise I'm not trying to be difficult. 

It's just... I really don't think I've been feeling sad for most of the day, you know? Like I mentioned before, I'm still getting up and going to work, and I still feel okay when I'm there. I wouldn't want you to write down that I'm just miserable all the time, because that's not really how it is. 

I guess I'm just... I'm more focused on how I've stopped doing my hobbies, like we just talked about. But the actual feeling sad part... no, I really don't think it's been happening like that. I hope that's okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you an accurate picture of what's going on, without making it seem like I'm completely helpless. Am I making sense?
Can you tell me if you have had several days in a row where you felt down or sad for most of the day, nearly every day, in the past two weeks?

Um... I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm frustrating you because you keep asking about feeling sad, and I keep giving the same answer. I really don't mean to be a difficult patient, I promise. 

It's just... I really haven't had several days in a row like that. I know I mentioned the hobbies and everything, but the actual feeling of being sad or down all day... I just haven't noticed that happening. I try really hard to keep a positive attitude, especially for my clients. I'd hate for anyone to think I'm just moping around all day, you know? 

I hope it's okay that I keep saying no to this one. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so you can do your job. Am I answering this okay? I'm really trying my best to be helpful.
Can you tell me if, over the past two weeks, there were several days when you felt down or sad for most of the day, even when things at work or home were going okay?

Oh, gosh... I feel so bad that we keep coming back to this. I really hope you don't think I'm being stubborn or trying to hide anything from you. I know you're just trying to get the full picture, and I want to be a good patient for you, I really do.

But... no, even when things are fine at work or at home, I just don't have those long stretches of feeling sad or down like that. I know I've lost interest in my painting and the theater stuff, which is still so embarrassing to admit, but the actual sadness... it just isn't there most of the day. 

I'm so sorry if that's not the answer you're looking for. I just really want to be honest with you so I don't give you the wrong impression about how I'm handling things. Is it okay that I just don't feel sad like that, even with the other stuff going on? I hope I'm still giving you what you need to figure this out.
Can you tell me if there have been times when, for two weeks or more, you felt down or sad for most of the day, nearly every day, even if only for a short period during that time?

Oh, I see, you mean like... ever? In the past? 

Um... gosh, I really hope I'm not messing up your evaluation by saying this, but... no, I don't think I've ever had a time like that either. Even looking back, I can't remember a stretch of two weeks where I was just sad all day. I've always prided myself on being a hard worker—with installing tile and flooring, you kind of just have to keep moving and stay upbeat for the clients, you know? I'd be so embarrassed if I ever let myself just sit around being sad for weeks on end. 

I'm really, really sorry, I feel like I'm failing this part of the interview because I keep giving you "no" for an answer. Am I still being helpful? I just genuinely don't remember ever feeling that way, and I want to make sure I'm doing exactly what you need me to do.
Can you tell me if there has ever been a time in your life when you felt down or lost interest in things for most of the day, more days than not, for a period lasting at least two weeks?

Oh, okay... the losing interest part. Yes, um... I know I keep saying no to the sadness, and I really hope I'm not making this difficult for you, but the losing interest... that part is definitely true. I'm a little embarrassed to even admit it, honestly, because I've always been such a go-getter. 

But... I used to do so much. I would paint, I'd cook these really big meals, I'd even go for a run before heading out to my flooring jobs, and I was always showing up for my theater rehearsals. But now... I don't know, those things just feel like chores from somebody else's life. I just... I really don't care if I miss them anymore. 

I know that sounds awful, and I really hope you don't think I'm just being lazy or giving up. I promise I try not to be like that. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm answering you right.
Can you tell me if, at any point in your life, you've had a period where you felt down or lost interest in things for most of the day, more days than not, for at least two weeks in a row?

Um... yes. This whole... losing interest thing... I guess this depression has actually been with me for a while now. I'm really embarrassed to admit how long it's been, because I know I should have just snapped out of it by now. I don't want you to think I'm weak or that I'm not trying my best to push through it. 

But... it's been about a year and two months. It started a few months after my husband's injury. I've really tried to keep a good face on for him, and for my clients at work, you know? I just kept hoping if I worked harder it would go away. 

I hope it's okay that I let it go on this long without getting help. I'm so sorry if I should have said something sooner. Am I giving you the right kind of timeline for your notes?
Can you tell me if, during that time when you lost interest in things, you also felt down or sad for most of the day, more days than not, for at least two weeks in a row?

Um... no. I know you asked me about feeling sad earlier, and I... I really don't want to sound like a broken record or like I'm being difficult. I promise I'm really thinking hard about it. 

But even during this past year and two months, when I stopped caring about my painting and the theater... I haven't really felt *sad*, exactly. Just... empty, I guess? Like I'm just going through the motions. I still get up and do my flooring jobs and take care of my husband, I just... I don't feel the joy in it anymore. But I wouldn't call it sadness. 

I'm so sorry, I know that's probably not the answer you're looking for, since you asked it again. I really hope I'm not messing up your diagnosis by not having the sadness part. Is it... is it okay that I just feel the loss of interest without the sadness? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Can you tell me if these feelings of losing interest in things and just going through the motions have been present for more than two years now?

Oh, um... no, not quite two years. I... I think I mentioned it just a minute ago, and I am so sorry if I mumbled or wasn't clear enough. I really don't mean to be confusing. 

It's been about a year and two months. Like I was saying, it started a few months after my husband's injury. I know a year and two months is still a really long time to let things slide, and I feel awful that I haven't been able to just bounce back and be my normal self yet... but it definitely hasn't been two whole years. 

I hope it's okay that I corrected you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the exact right dates so I don't mess up your notes. Am I doing okay with these questions?
